header.title: How to Change a Washing Machine Belt
header.description: This guide provides step-by-step instructions on how to replace a worn or damaged washing machine belt. Follow these instructions to safely diagnose, remove, and install a new belt to restore your washing machine's functionality.

steps.description: This step involves preparing the washing machine for repair by disconnecting utilities, clearing obstructions, and positioning it for access to the belt assembly.
actions: Unplug the washing machine from the outlet.
Disconnect the water supply and hoses.
Turn off the water by closing the supply shut-off valves.
Remove the hoses (have a bucket nearby).
Remove the drain hose from where it feeds into.
Unclog any articles of clothing from the drum.
Remove any clothing inside the machine.
Drain the machine (refer to manual for proper procedure).
Move the washing machine back, forward, or on its side to access the panel.
Locate the panel access first.
Lay an old blanket, towels, or cardboard down to protect the floor or machine feet.
Tilt the machine to get a visual.
Use bricks, paint cans, or sturdy objects to lift the machine for a quick look.

steps.description: This step instructs the user to remove the access panel from the machine, potentially requiring access from the bottom.
actions: Find the access panel
Remove the cover from the unit
Check for screws holding the cover
Check for latches holding the cover
If necessary, lay the machine on its side
Remove the bottom panel

steps.description: Locate the washing machine belt, noting its placement and condition, and documenting the access steps for reinstallation.
actions: Remove the access panel.
Locate the belt (check back for front-loading machines, bottom for top-loading machines).
Consult your manual or contact the manufacturer if no belt is found.
Make a mental note or draw a diagram of the belt's placement.
Write down the steps you took to access the belt.
Inspect the belt for damage (stretched, frayed, cracked, melted).
If the belt is damaged, replace it.
If the belt has slipped off its housing, try pushing it back into place.

steps.description: Re-attach the belt by removing the pump coupling, slipping off the old belt, and replacing it on the pulleys, potentially loosening motor mount bolts for slack.
actions: Locate the pump coupling.
Remove the pump coupling.
Slip off the existing belt.
Replace the belt on the pulleys.
Loosen the bolts of the motor mount (if needed).

steps.description: This step involves sourcing a replacement washing machine belt and installing it according to the manufacturer's specifications, ensuring proper tension and alignment.
actions: Source a new washing machine belt online or at an appliance parts supplier.
Verify the replacement belt is manufactured for older models, if applicable.
Consult the manufacturer or appliance manual to source the exact belt specified.
Put the new belt on following the diagram pattern or reversing the removal process.
Ensure the flat side of the belt faces out and the grooved side faces in.
Place part of the belt on the drum pulley so that it fits into the grooves.
Attach the other end to the motor pulley.
Have someone turn the drum by hand to help work the belt into the proper position.
Rotate the drum at least one full rotation to secure the belt.
Adjust the belt to have no more than ½ inch of slack.
Replace the pump coupling.
Re-tighten the motor mount bolts.
Apply light pressure on the belt with the handle of a hammer if adjustment is difficult.

steps.description: This step involves reassembling the washing machine, connecting water lines, and restoring electrical power.
actions: Put the access panel back on with the screws or latches
Move the machine back to where you can restore the electrical and water supplies
Remove any paint cans or wedges
Get it level with the floor again
Attach the water supply hoses
Put the drain hose back into position
Turn the water supply back on
Check for leaks
Plug the electrical cord back into the wall
Position the washing machine in its permanent place

steps.description: Test the washing machine to ensure it is functioning correctly after repairs.
actions: Consult the manual for test run instructions.
Put in a small load of clothing.
Do a regular cycle.
Listen closely to the machine.
Stop the machine immediately if it shakes excessively or smells burning.
Let the cycle finish while observing the machine.
Check the clothes for cleanliness and dryness.
Call a professional if clothes are wet, soapy, or not cleaned properly.
